questions.explanation: Once a discrete GPU is installed, onboard video is often disabled, so the monitor must use the new card's ports.

questions.prompt: A phone charges only intermittently, even with a new cable and charger. What should the technician check NEXT?
questions.explanation: Lint packed into the charging port often blocks a solid connection; cleaning it is quick and non-invasive.

questions.prompt: A laptop's built-in screen is black, but an external monitor connected to it displays normally. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: A fault in the laptop's display hardware
questions.explanation: Because the GPU and OS work on the external display, the fault is in the laptop's own display hardware.

questions.prompt: After a drop, a tablet ignores touch in one area even though the image displays normally. What part MOST likely needs replacement?
questions.explanation: The digitizer handles touch input, so a dead touch zone with a normal image points to it.

questions.prompt: A user dropped a phone into water and it still appears to work. What should be advised FIRST?
choices: Charge it fully to test the battery
Place it in a hot oven to dry
Power it off and do not charge it
questions.explanation: Powering off and not charging reduces the risk of short circuits while the device dries or is serviced.

questions.prompt: A laser printer prints faint duplicate images of earlier content lower on each page. Which component is MOST likely at fault?
questions.explanation: Ghost images usually come from an imaging drum that is not being fully cleaned or discharged between rotations.

questions.prompt: A printer in a humid storage room keeps jamming, and pages come out wrinkled. What is the BEST fix?
questions.explanation: Damp paper curls and sticks together, causing jams and wrinkles; it should be stored in a dry place.

questions.prompt: A printer outputs pages of random symbols and garbled characters. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Garbled output means the printer is getting data it cannot interpret, typically from a wrong or corrupt driver.

questions.prompt: After an office network change, users can no longer print to a network printer whose IP address changed. What is the BEST long-term fix?
choices: Switch all users to USB printing
Reinstall the operating system on each PC
Reserve the printer's IP and update the port
questions.explanation: A DHCP reservation keeps the printer's address fixed, and updating the printer port points PCs to it.

questions.prompt: A user can ping 127.0.0.1 but not the default gateway. What does this indicate?
choices: The remote website is currently down
The DNS server for the office is offline
The TCP/IP stack on the PC is corrupted
The local stack works, but the link or config is faulty
questions.explanation: A successful loopback ping proves the local stack is fine, so the fault lies in the cable, NIC, switch or configuration.

questions.prompt: A PC can reach shares on the local network but not the internet. ipconfig shows no default gateway. What should be done?
questions.explanation: Without a default gateway, traffic cannot leave the local subnet to reach the internet.

questions.prompt: A laptop's Wi-Fi drops whenever the break room microwave is running. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Connect the laptop to the 5 GHz band
Move the laptop closer to the microwave
questions.explanation: Microwave ovens interfere with 2.4 GHz; the 5 GHz band avoids that interference.

questions.prompt: A cable tester shows one pair as open on a newly installed run. What should the technician do?
questions.explanation: An open pair means a broken or poorly seated wire, usually fixed by re-terminating the connector.

questions.prompt: A PC connected with a 130-meter Cat 6 run has frequent errors and slow throughput. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: An incorrect subnet mask on the PC
questions.explanation: Copper Ethernet runs are limited to 100 meters; longer runs suffer signal loss and errors.

questions.prompt: One drive in a two-drive RAID 0 array has failed. What is the outcome?
choices: The remaining drive keeps a full mirrored copy
The array runs in degraded mode until rebuilt
Parity data rebuilds the failed drive automatically
The array is lost and data must be restored from backup
questions.explanation: RAID 0 has no redundancy, so losing any one drive destroys the whole array.

questions.prompt: A newly added second drive does not appear in File Explorer, but Disk Management shows it as unallocated. What should be done?
choices: Initialize the disk and create a volume
Run the System File Checker tool
questions.explanation: A new drive must be initialized, partitioned and formatted before Windows assigns it a drive letter.

questions.prompt: After reinstalling a CPU cooler, a PC shuts off a few minutes after boot. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The cooler is poorly seated or lacks paste
The RAM is running in single-channel mode
The hard drive has bad sectors
questions.explanation: Poor cooler contact causes the CPU to overheat quickly, triggering thermal shutdown.

questions.prompt: An office PC is running loud and slow, and monitoring software shows high CPU temperatures. The vents are clogged. What should the technician do?
choices: Blow out the dust with compressed air
questions.explanation: Dust blocks airflow, causing overheating and throttling; cleaning restores cooling.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command lists active TCP connections and the ports the computer is listening on?
questions.explanation: netstat shows active connections and listening ports; adding -b shows which program owns each one.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command displays only the computer's name?
questions.explanation: hostname prints the computer name; whoami shows the logged-in user account.

questions.prompt: Which command restarts a Windows PC immediately with no delay?
questions.explanation: shutdown /r restarts the PC, and /t 0 sets the delay to zero seconds.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to quickly confirm which Windows version and build a PC is running. Which command opens that information?
questions.explanation: winver opens the About Windows dialog showing the edition, version and build number.

questions.prompt: A technician wants a PC to start in Safe Mode on its next restart from within Windows. Which tool provides a Safe boot option?
questions.explanation: The Boot tab in msconfig has a Safe boot checkbox that applies on the next restart.

questions.prompt: Which Windows tool lets a technician directly view and edit the hierarchical database of system and application settings?
questions.explanation: regedit edits the Windows Registry; changes should be made carefully and backed up first.

questions.prompt: A newly updated network driver causes connection drops. Where can the technician revert to the previous driver?
questions.explanation: Device Manager's Roll Back Driver option on the driver tab restores the previously installed driver.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to extend a Windows data volume into adjacent unallocated space using a graphical tool. Which tool should be used?
questions.explanation: Disk Management can create, extend, shrink and format volumes and assign drive letters.

questions.prompt: A technician wants to log CPU and disk counters over several days to find a performance pattern. Which tool is BEST?
questions.explanation: Performance Monitor can collect counter data over time with data collector sets; Task Manager shows only live data.

questions.prompt: Which Windows tool gives a detailed inventory of hardware resources, components and the software environment?
questions.explanation: msinfo32 summarizes hardware, IRQs, components and drivers in one report.

questions.prompt: A user has graphics and sound problems in a game. Which Windows tool reports DirectX, display and audio driver details?
questions.explanation: The DirectX Diagnostic Tool lists display and sound devices, drivers and DirectX features.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to view and import a user's personal digital certificates in Windows. Which console should be opened?
questions.explanation: certmgr.msc manages the current user's certificate store.

questions.prompt: On a standalone Windows Pro PC, which tool sets local policies such as password rules and software restrictions?
questions.explanation: gpedit.msc edits local policies on Pro and higher editions; Home editions do not include it.

questions.prompt: A user's PC is low on space from temporary files and the Recycle Bin. Which built-in tool safely removes these?
questions.explanation: Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr) deletes temporary files, cached update files and the Recycle Bin contents.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum RAM required to install Windows 11?
questions.explanation: Windows 11 requires at least 4 GB of RAM and 64 GB of storage, along with TPM 2.0 and UEFI Secure Boot support.

questions.prompt: A PC has 16 GB of RAM installed, but Windows shows less than 4 GB usable. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: A 32-bit version of Windows is installed
The RAM is running in dual-channel mode
questions.explanation: A 32-bit OS can address only about 4 GB of memory; a 64-bit OS is needed to use more.

questions.prompt: A technician is partitioning a new 4 TB drive and wants to use all of its space. Why is MBR a poor choice?
choices: MBR supports disks only up to 2 TB
MBR requires UEFI firmware to boot
MBR does not work with NTFS
questions.explanation: MBR is limited to 2 TB and four primary partitions; GPT supports far larger disks.

questions.prompt: A user wants to reinstall Windows on a sluggish PC while keeping personal files. Which built-in option fits BEST?
choices: Reset this PC with Keep my files
Format the drive and clean install
questions.explanation: Reset this PC reinstalls Windows and can keep personal files while removing apps and settings.

questions.prompt: A five-person office with no server wants to share files between Windows PCs. Which network model should be used?
questions.explanation: A workgroup is a peer-to-peer model where each PC manages its own accounts, suitable for small offices with no server.

questions.prompt: Which hidden administrative share gives administrators remote access to the root of a Windows PC's system drive?
questions.explanation: Windows automatically creates hidden admin shares like C$ for the root of each drive.

questions.prompt: A user connects a Windows laptop to a phone hotspot and wants to limit background downloads. Which setting should be enabled?
questions.explanation: Marking a network as metered reduces background data use such as some updates and syncing.

questions.prompt: Which macOS feature shows all open windows and lets the user create additional virtual desktops called Spaces?
questions.explanation: Mission Control displays open windows and manages multiple desktops (Spaces).

questions.prompt: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Force Quit Applications window on macOS?
questions.explanation: Command+Option+Escape opens Force Quit, similar to ending a task in Windows Task Manager.

questions.prompt: A Mac user downloaded an app as a disk image they must open and drag to Applications. Which file extension is it?
questions.explanation: macOS apps are often distributed as .dmg disk images; .msi and .exe are Windows installers.

questions.prompt: Which command displays IP addresses for network interfaces on a modern Linux system?
questions.explanation: ip addr (part of the ip utility) shows interface addresses on Linux; ipconfig is the Windows equivalent.

questions.prompt: A Linux user wants to read the built-in documentation for the chmod command. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: The man command opens the manual page for a Linux command.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command is used to rename a file?
questions.explanation: mv moves or renames files; cp copies them and leaves the original in place.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to edit a configuration file from a Linux terminal with a simple text editor. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: nano is a simple terminal text editor; grep searches text and df reports disk space.

questions.prompt: Which WPA3 feature replaces the pre-shared key handshake to resist offline dictionary attacks?
questions.explanation: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE) protects against offline password guessing better than WPA2-PSK.

questions.prompt: Which encryption method does WPA2 use for strong wireless security?
questions.explanation: WPA2 uses AES with CCMP; TKIP is older and weaker.

questions.prompt: Which authentication protocol do Windows domains use by default, issuing tickets from the domain controller?
questions.explanation: Active Directory uses Kerberos, which issues time-limited tickets to authenticate users and services.

questions.prompt: Which AAA protocol, common for network device administration, uses TCP and separates authentication, authorization and accounting?
questions.explanation: TACACS+ uses TCP and handles each AAA function separately; RADIUS uses UDP and combines authentication and authorization.

questions.prompt: Which type of malware secretly monitors a user's activity and sends information such as browsing habits to a third party?
questions.explanation: Spyware collects data about the user without consent and sends it to the attacker.

questions.prompt: Which type of malware records each key a user presses to capture passwords?
questions.explanation: A keylogger captures keystrokes, often to steal credentials; it can be software or a hardware device.

questions.prompt: Thousands of infected home PCs are controlled remotely by an attacker to send spam. What are these PCs part of?
questions.explanation: A botnet is a network of compromised computers controlled by an attacker through command-and-control servers.

questions.prompt: A PC's CPU runs at 100% all day due to hidden software using its resources to generate digital currency for an attacker. What type of malware is this?
questions.explanation: Cryptominers hijack computing power to mine cryptocurrency, causing high resource usage.

questions.prompt: A phishing email is crafted specifically to target a company's CFO. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Whaling is spear phishing aimed at high-level executives.

questions.prompt: An attacker searches through a company's trash to find printed passwords and network diagrams. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Dumpster diving recovers sensitive information from discarded materials, which is why shredding policies matter.

questions.prompt: A website is overwhelmed by traffic from thousands of compromised devices at once. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: A distributed denial-of-service attack uses many sources to flood a target and make it unavailable.

questions.prompt: An attacker injects malicious script into a website comment field so it runs in other visitors' browsers. What attack is this?
questions.explanation: XSS injects client-side scripts into web pages viewed by other users; SQL injection targets the database.

questions.prompt: A receptionist's monitor faces the lobby and visitors can read the screen. Which control BEST reduces this risk?
questions.explanation: A privacy filter narrows the viewing angle so only the person in front of the screen can read it.

questions.prompt: Which physical control uses short, sturdy posts to stop vehicles from driving into a building entrance?
questions.explanation: Bollards are barriers that block vehicles while allowing pedestrians through.

questions.prompt: Laptops in a public computer lab are being stolen from desks. Which control is the BEST low-cost fix?
questions.explanation: Cable locks physically attach laptops to furniture; encryption protects data but does not prevent theft.

questions.prompt: A company wants to stop malware from launching automatically when USB drives are inserted. Which setting should be disabled?
questions.explanation: Disabling AutoRun and AutoPlay prevents removable media from running code automatically when connected.

questions.prompt: Which Windows feature encrypts removable USB flash drives?
questions.explanation: BitLocker To Go extends BitLocker encryption to removable drives.

questions.prompt: A user wants to encrypt a single folder on an NTFS drive so it can be read only by their own account. Which feature should be used?
questions.explanation: The Encrypting File System encrypts individual files and folders tied to the user's account; BitLocker encrypts whole volumes.

questions.prompt: A laptop joins a coffee shop's Wi-Fi network. Which Windows Defender Firewall profile should be applied for the strictest settings?
questions.explanation: The Public profile is the most restrictive and should be used on untrusted networks.

questions.prompt: Users often leave their desks with their PCs unlocked. Which control BEST addresses this?
choices: An automatic screen lock after inactivity
questions.explanation: An inactivity timeout locks the screen automatically when a user forgets to.

questions.prompt: A company wants a lost phone's data protected if someone repeatedly guesses the passcode. Which policy should be configured?
choices: Wipe the device after repeated failed unlocks
Allow only cellular data on the device
questions.explanation: A failed-attempt limit that triggers a wipe stops brute-force guessing of the passcode.

questions.prompt: Which SOHO router feature should be disabled because its PIN method can be brute-forced?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Setup's PIN method is vulnerable to brute-force attacks, so it should be turned off.

questions.prompt: Which ongoing task BEST protects a SOHO router against newly discovered vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: Firmware updates patch security flaws in the router's software.

questions.prompt: Which SOHO router control lets only devices with specific hardware addresses join the network, though it can be spoofed?
questions.explanation: MAC filtering allows or denies devices by MAC address, but attackers can spoof allowed addresses.

questions.prompt: A technician downloads a browser installer and wants to confirm it was not tampered with. What should be done?
choices: Rename the file before running it
Run the installer in compatibility mode
Check that the file name matches the vendor
Compare its hash with the vendor's published hash
questions.explanation: A matching hash value confirms the file's integrity against what the vendor published.

questions.prompt: A user on a shared library computer does not want browsing history or cookies kept after the session. Which feature should be used?
questions.explanation: Private or incognito mode discards history, cookies and form data when the window closes.

questions.prompt: Employees reuse the same weak password on many websites. Which tool BEST helps them use unique strong passwords?
questions.explanation: Password managers generate and securely store unique complex passwords for each site.

questions.prompt: An attacker tries thousands of common words and leaked passwords from a list against a login. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: A dictionary attack uses a word list of likely passwords instead of trying every possible combination.

questions.prompt: A Windows service fails to start, and the error says a dependency service failed to start. What should the technician check?
choices: The amount of free disk space
questions.explanation: A service will not start if a required dependency is stopped or disabled; the Dependencies tab lists them.

questions.prompt: A USB scanner shows as an unknown device with a yellow warning in Device Manager. What should be done?
choices: Install or update the device driver
Run Disk Cleanup to free space
Change the power plan to High performance
questions.explanation: A yellow warning indicates a driver problem, so installing the correct driver usually fixes it.

questions.prompt: A PC with a mechanical drive has become very slow, and the drive is 98% full. What should be done FIRST?
questions.explanation: Nearly full drives leave little room for the page file and temporary files; freeing space is the first, least invasive step.

questions.prompt: A user with two monitors must move the mouse off the right edge of one screen to reach the other, which sits on the left. How should this be fixed?
choices: Swap the video cables between GPUs
questions.explanation: Display settings let you drag the monitor icons to match their physical layout.

questions.prompt: According to CompTIA's malware removal procedure, what should be done right after investigating and verifying the malware symptoms?
questions.explanation: After verifying symptoms, the infected system is quarantined to stop the spread before further steps.

questions.prompt: What is the LAST step in CompTIA's malware removal procedure?
choices: Enable System Restore and create a restore point
questions.explanation: After re-enabling System Restore and creating a restore point, the final step is user education to prevent reinfection.

questions.prompt: A pop-up claiming to be antivirus software reports dozens of infections and demands payment to clean them. What is this MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Fake antivirus pop-ups use scare tactics to trick users into paying or installing more malware.

questions.prompt: A PC goes to a fake site when a user types a bank's correct web address, but other PCs reach it fine. Which file should be checked for malicious entries?
questions.explanation: Malware can add entries to the hosts file to redirect specific domains to attacker-controlled IP addresses.

questions.prompt: A user's contacts report receiving spam that appears to come from the user's email account. What is the BEST first step?
choices: Reset the password and enable MFA
questions.explanation: Spam sent from the account indicates it is compromised; resetting credentials and adding MFA stops further misuse.

questions.prompt: A phone has become sluggish and apps open slowly, and settings show storage almost full. What should be done FIRST?
questions.explanation: Low storage slows mobile devices; clearing space is quick and non-destructive.

questions.prompt: A phone no longer connects to a Bluetooth car stereo it used to pair with. What should be tried FIRST?
choices: Remove the pairing and pair again
questions.explanation: Removing and re-creating the pairing clears corrupted pairing data.

questions.prompt: An app loads data on Wi-Fi but shows 'no connection' on cellular, while other apps work on cellular. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Cellular data is off for that app
The phone's SIM card is damaged
The app needs a factory reset
questions.explanation: Phones let users block cellular data per app; since other apps work, that setting is the likely cause.

questions.prompt: An MDM console flags an employee's phone because its built-in OS restrictions have been removed to allow unauthorized software. What has happened?
choices: The device is in airplane mode
questions.explanation: Rooting or jailbreaking bypasses OS security controls, so MDM policies often block such devices.

questions.prompt: An Android phone began showing ads everywhere after the user installed an app downloaded from a website instead of the app store. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Installing APKs from unknown sources bypasses store vetting and is a common route for adware and malware.

questions.prompt: A user installs a free flashlight app that requests access to contacts, microphone and location. What should the technician advise?
choices: Restart the phone to reset permissions
Turn on airplane mode while using it
Uninstall the app due to its excessive permissions
Grant the permissions so the light works
questions.explanation: A flashlight does not need contacts or location; excessive permission requests are a warning sign of data-harvesting apps.

questions.prompt: An older business application fails to run correctly on Windows 11 but worked on an older version. What should be tried FIRST?
questions.explanation: Compatibility mode emulates an earlier Windows version and can let older apps run on newer systems.

questions.prompt: Domain users on one PC get login errors, and the PC's clock is 20 minutes off from the domain controller. What should be done?
choices: Rejoin the PC to a workgroup
Sync the PC's clock with the domain
questions.explanation: Kerberos requires clocks to be closely synchronized; large time differences cause authentication failures.

questions.prompt: A user complains that Windows restarts to install updates while they are working during the day. What should be configured?
questions.explanation: Active hours tell Windows when the user is usually working so it avoids automatic restarts then.

questions.prompt: Malware keeps returning after every removal attempt while Windows is running normally. What should the technician try?
choices: Increase the size of the page file
Scan from Safe Mode or a boot environment
questions.explanation: Running scans outside the normal OS stops the malware from loading and protecting itself.

questions.prompt: After logging in, a Windows user sees only a black screen with a mouse cursor. What can the technician try FIRST?
questions.explanation: A black screen with a cursor often means Explorer failed to load; starting explorer.exe from Task Manager restores the desktop.

questions.prompt: A phone no longer connects to the home Wi-Fi after the router's password was changed. What should be done?
choices: Reset all phone settings to factory
Forget the network and rejoin it
questions.explanation: The phone keeps trying the saved old password; forgetting the network lets the user enter the new one.

questions.prompt: Windows shows 'Your system is low on virtual memory' even though plenty of disk space exists. What should be checked?
choices: Whether the paging file is disabled or too small
Whether the monitor's refresh rate is correct
questions.explanation: Virtual memory depends on the paging file; if it is disabled or capped too low, Windows reports low virtual memory.

questions.prompt: A user says their phone has stopped ringing for calls, though calls appear as missed. What should be checked FIRST?
choices: Whether the SIM card is damaged
Whether Do Not Disturb is enabled
questions.explanation: Do Not Disturb or focus modes silence incoming calls while still logging them as missed.

questions.prompt: Which ticket field ranks how urgently an issue must be handled based on its business impact?
questions.explanation: Priority, based on impact and urgency, determines response order and SLA timing.

questions.prompt: A company wants to track who has each laptop and when its warranty expires. What should be used?
choices: Asset tags and an inventory system
questions.explanation: Asset tags linked to an inventory database record ownership, location and warranty details.

questions.prompt: A technician solves a tricky printer issue and wants others to fix it faster next time. What should be created?
questions.explanation: Knowledge base articles document solutions so other technicians can reuse them.

questions.prompt: In change management, which group reviews and approves or rejects proposed changes?
questions.explanation: The change advisory board (CAB) evaluates risk and impact before approving a change.

questions.prompt: Before rolling out a major software update to all users, what should be done to reduce risk?
choices: Install it only on executives' PCs
Deploy it to everyone at once
Test it in a sandbox environment first
questions.explanation: Testing in an isolated environment finds problems before they affect production users.

questions.prompt: Which backup type combines an earlier full backup with later incremental backups to build a new full backup without reading the source again?
questions.explanation: A synthetic full is assembled from existing backup data, reducing load on the production system.

questions.prompt: An office runs nightly backups but has never tried restoring from them. What is the BEST recommendation?
questions.explanation: Only test restores prove that backups are complete and recoverable.

questions.prompt: Which backup rotation scheme uses daily, weekly and monthly backup sets?
questions.explanation: In GFS, son backups are daily, father backups are weekly and grandfather backups are monthly.

questions.prompt: A power supply has failed in a desktop. What is the SAFEST approach?
choices: Use an ESD strap while repairing the inside
Open it while it is plugged in to test
Replace the whole unit rather than opening it
Open it and replace the capacitors
questions.explanation: PSUs hold dangerous charges in their capacitors even when unplugged, so they are replaced, not repaired.

questions.prompt: Which class of fire extinguisher is used for electrical fires in the United States?
questions.explanation: Class C extinguishers, such as CO2, are rated for energized electrical equipment; Class A is for ordinary combustibles.

questions.prompt: Why is very low humidity a concern in a room full of computer equipment?
choices: It causes condensation on circuit boards
It increases the risk of static discharge
It raises the risk of corrosion
questions.explanation: Dry air allows static charge to build up, raising ESD risk; high humidity causes condensation.

questions.prompt: How should an empty laser printer toner cartridge be disposed of?
choices: Burn it to destroy the toner
Throw it in the regular office trash
Recycle it according to local regulations
Empty the residue into a sink
questions.explanation: Toner cartridges should be recycled or returned per local regulations and the SDS guidance.

questions.prompt: Which device protects equipment from voltage spikes but does not provide power during an outage?
questions.explanation: A surge suppressor blocks spikes; a UPS adds battery power for outages.

questions.prompt: Which document is the legal agreement that sets how a user may use a piece of software?
questions.explanation: The end-user license agreement defines software usage rights and restrictions.

questions.prompt: Which regulation governs how organizations handle the personal data of people in the European Union?
questions.explanation: The General Data Protection Regulation sets rules for collecting and processing EU residents' personal data.

questions.prompt: A technician is explaining a repair to a non-technical customer. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Use technical terms to show expertise
Use plain language and avoid jargon
questions.explanation: Clear, non-technical language helps customers understand and builds trust.

questions.prompt: A repair will take longer than expected because a part is on backorder. What should the technician do?
choices: Install a used part without asking
Close the ticket and reopen it later
Inform the customer and give a new timeline
Wait until the part arrives to say anything
questions.explanation: Setting and updating expectations keeps the customer informed and avoids frustration.

questions.prompt: Which file extension is used for Windows batch scripts?
questions.explanation: .bat files run commands in the Windows command interpreter; .sh is for Unix shells and .ps1 for PowerShell.

questions.prompt: A managed service provider wants to monitor client PCs, push patches and run scripts remotely from one console. Which tool fits BEST?
questions.explanation: RMM platforms combine monitoring, patching, scripting and remote control for many endpoints.

questions.prompt: An employee wants to paste customer records into a public AI chatbot to summarize them. What is the MAIN concern?
choices: Sensitive data may be exposed to others
The chatbot cannot read text input
The chatbot will slow down the network
The summary will be too short to use
questions.explanation: Public AI tools may store or use submitted data, so company policy should prohibit entering sensitive information.

questions.prompt: An AI assistant gives a confident answer that includes a command that does not exist. What is this called?
questions.explanation: AI hallucinations are plausible-sounding but incorrect outputs, so AI answers should be verified before use.

questions.prompt: A file server must keep running even if any two of its drives fail at the same time. Which RAID level should be configured?
questions.explanation: RAID 6 uses dual distributed parity, needs at least four drives and tolerates two simultaneous drive failures. RAID 5 survives only one.

questions.prompt: A technician connects a SATA SSD to a SATA III port. What is the maximum theoretical interface speed of that connection?
questions.explanation: SATA III (SATA 6Gb/s) has a maximum interface rate of 6 Gbps; 1.5 and 3 Gbps are SATA I and II.

questions.prompt: In the laser printing process, which step places a uniform negative charge on the imaging drum before the image is written?
questions.explanation: During charging, the primary charge roller or corona wire applies a uniform negative charge to the drum so the laser can then discharge the image areas.

questions.prompt: An administrator wants to use one keyboard, mouse and monitor to control two desktop computers on the same desk. Which device should be installed?
questions.explanation: A KVM (keyboard, video, mouse) switch lets one set of peripherals control multiple computers by switching between them.

questions.prompt: Which CPU architecture is used in most smartphones and in Apple silicon Macs, chosen largely for its power efficiency?
questions.explanation: ARM is a RISC architecture known for low power use and is used in most mobile devices and Apple silicon. x86-64 dominates traditional PCs.

questions.prompt: Confidential HR printouts are often left sitting in a shared printer's output tray. Which printer feature BEST prevents this?
choices: Duplex printing set as the default for all users
Secured print requiring a PIN or badge to release jobs
A larger output tray fitted with a locking privacy cover
Printing to a file and emailing it instead
questions.explanation: Secured print (print release) holds the job until the user authenticates at the device, so documents are not left unattended.

questions.prompt: A laser printer no longer feeds paper; the sheets stay in the tray and the rubber rollers look shiny and smooth. Which part should be replaced?
questions.explanation: Worn, glazed pickup rollers lose grip and fail to pull paper from the tray. The separation pad problem is the opposite, pulling several sheets.

questions.prompt: After a CMOS reset, a Windows PC fails to boot with an INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE error. Nothing else changed. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The CMOS battery is now completely drained
Secure Boot keys were erased and must be re-enrolled
The boot drive failed during the CMOS reset
The SATA mode (AHCI/RAID) no longer matches the original
questions.explanation: Resetting UEFI settings can revert the SATA controller mode (for example between RAID/Intel RST and AHCI), and Windows then cannot load the right storage driver. Restoring the original mode fixes it.

questions.prompt: VoIP users report choppy audio because packets arrive with uneven delays between them. Which network issue does this describe?
questions.explanation: Jitter is variation in packet delay, which disrupts real-time traffic like voice and video. Attenuation is signal loss over distance.

questions.prompt: Text on a new LCD monitor looks blurry and slightly stretched, although the cable and drivers are fine. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Replace the video cable with a shielded one
Degauss the monitor from its menu
Lower the refresh rate to reduce flicker
questions.explanation: LCDs look sharp only at their native resolution; other resolutions are scaled and appear fuzzy. Degaussing applies to old CRTs.

questions.prompt: A technician wants to check whether a desktop power supply is outputting correct voltages on its connectors without installing it in another PC. Which tool should be used?
questions.explanation: A power supply tester plugs into the PSU's connectors and shows whether each rail is within specification. A multimeter can also measure voltages.

questions.prompt: A laptop is connected to a conference room projector by HDMI, but only the laptop screen shows an image. What should the technician try FIRST?
choices: Replace the HDMI cable with a new one
Update the laptop's BIOS and chipset
questions.explanation: Windows+P switches the projection mode; if it is set to PC screen only, the external display receives no image. Check the simple setting before replacing hardware.

questions.prompt: During phone calls, a user's smartphone screen stays on and their cheek keeps pressing the mute button. A new thick screen protector was just applied. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The ambient light sensor has been disabled
questions.explanation: The proximity sensor turns the screen off when the phone is held to the ear; covering it with a screen protector stops this from working.

questions.prompt: On a laptop, pressing F5 changes the screen brightness instead of refreshing the web page. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The browser does not support F5
Fn lock is reversing the function keys
The keyboard driver is corrupt or outdated
questions.explanation: Many laptops let the top row act as media keys by default; toggling Fn lock (or the BIOS function key setting) restores standard F1-F12 behavior.

questions.prompt: A laptop that worked on Wi-Fi before a flight now shows no wireless networks at all. Device Manager shows the wireless card working with no errors. What should be checked FIRST?
choices: Whether the display's antenna leads are disconnected
Whether the router's SSID is hidden
Whether airplane mode or the wireless toggle is on
Whether the WLAN card needs replacing
questions.explanation: Airplane mode or a hardware wireless switch disables the radio while the device still appears healthy. It is the quickest, most likely cause after travel.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to securely transfer files to a Linux server using SFTP. Which port must be allowed through the firewall?
questions.explanation: SFTP runs over SSH, which uses TCP port 22. Port 21 is plain FTP control and UDP 69 is TFTP.

questions.prompt: Which ports are associated with NetBIOS over TCP/IP, used by older Windows name resolution and file sharing?
questions.explanation: NetBIOS uses ports 137 to 139 for name, datagram and session services. Modern SMB runs directly over TCP 445.

questions.prompt: A remote cabin uses a traditional geostationary satellite internet service. Which problem are users MOST likely to notice compared with fiber?
choices: High latency for video calls and gaming
Speeds limited to dial-up modem rates
Inability to obtain an address from DHCP
questions.explanation: Signals travel to a satellite about 36,000 km up and back, adding substantial latency that hurts real-time applications.

questions.prompt: A data center wants servers to access shared block-level storage over a dedicated high-speed network. Which network type is this?
questions.explanation: A storage area network (SAN) provides block-level access to storage over a dedicated network. A NAS provides file-level shares.

questions.prompt: A technician is making custom-length patch cables and needs to attach RJ45 connectors to the cable ends. Which tool is required?
questions.explanation: A crimper presses the RJ45 connector's pins onto the wires. A punchdown tool terminates wires into patch panels and keystone jacks.

questions.prompt: A company moves to a new hosted email provider, and outside senders' messages must be delivered to it. Which DNS record must be updated?
questions.explanation: MX (mail exchanger) records tell other mail servers where to deliver email for the domain. PTR records are used for reverse lookups.

questions.prompt: A Linux administrator needs to locate a file named backup.conf somewhere under /etc. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: find searches a directory tree for files matching criteria such as name. grep searches inside file contents.

questions.prompt: A Linux user wants a one-time snapshot list of all running processes, including those of other users. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: ps reports currently running processes, and aux shows all users' processes with details. top shows a continuously updating view.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to install a package on a Fedora or Red Hat Enterprise Linux system. Which package manager command should be used?
questions.explanation: dnf is the package manager for Fedora and modern RHEL-based distributions. apt is used on Debian and Ubuntu.

questions.prompt: From an elevated command prompt, a technician needs to create a local Windows user account named jsmith. Which command does this?
questions.explanation: net user with /add creates a local account, and the asterisk prompts for the password. net use maps network drives.

questions.prompt: A company requires that the startup disk of every MacBook be fully encrypted. Which built-in macOS feature should be enabled?
questions.explanation: FileVault provides full-disk encryption on macOS. Gatekeeper controls which apps may run, and Time Machine handles backups.

questions.prompt: A user wants to connect to their home desktop with Remote Desktop from work, but the desktop runs Windows 11 Home. What is the BEST solution?
choices: Install the Remote Desktop app on the work PC
Enable Remote Assistance and use RDP
Upgrade the desktop to Windows 11 Pro
Open TCP 3389 on the home router
questions.explanation: Windows Home can act as an RDP client but not as a Remote Desktop host. Opening ports will not help without the host feature, which Pro provides.

questions.prompt: After a password change, a Windows PC keeps failing to reconnect a mapped drive because it uses an old saved password. Which tool should be used to remove the cached entry?
questions.explanation: Credential Manager stores saved Windows and web credentials and lets a technician edit or remove stale entries.

questions.prompt: A small tablet PC with only a 32 GB internal drive fails the Windows 11 compatibility check. Which requirement is it missing?
choices: At least 256 GB of SSD storage
questions.explanation: Microsoft lists 64 GB or larger storage as a minimum requirement for Windows 11, along with 4 GB RAM and TPM 2.0.

questions.prompt: After a laptop's motherboard was replaced, Windows asks for a BitLocker recovery key at startup. What should the technician do?
choices: Clear the CMOS so the new TPM can import the old keys
Enter the recovery key from the user's backup location
Boot into Safe Mode, which bypasses BitLocker entirely
Reinstall Windows to remove BitLocker from the drive
questions.explanation: The new TPM does not hold the old keys, so BitLocker requires the 48-digit recovery key, typically stored in the Microsoft account, AD or Entra ID.

questions.prompt: A company hires a vendor to destroy old hard drives off-site. What should the company obtain to prove the drives were properly destroyed?
choices: A copy of the vendor's acceptable use policy
A chain of custody form signed by IT only
questions.explanation: A certificate of destruction documents that the media were destroyed and when, providing proof for audits and compliance.

questions.prompt: Old office PCs will be donated to a school, and their hard drives must remain usable but contain no recoverable data. What is the BEST method?
choices: Perform a standard quick format of each drive
Degauss the drives with a strong magnet
Drill through the platters of each drive
Overwrite them with a secure wiping utility
questions.explanation: Secure wiping overwrites data so it cannot be recovered while leaving the drive usable. Degaussing and drilling make the drive unusable, and a quick format leaves data recoverable.

questions.prompt: A department still uses a PC running an operating system that the vendor no longer supports with security updates. What is the MAIN risk?
choices: New vulnerabilities will never be patched
The PC will stop booting after the end date
The PC cannot join a network
questions.explanation: End-of-life operating systems no longer receive patches, so newly discovered vulnerabilities remain exploitable.

questions.prompt: A company is choosing a second factor for staff logins. Which option is MOST vulnerable to SIM-swapping attacks?
choices: One-time codes sent by SMS text message
questions.explanation: SMS codes go to whoever controls the phone number, so an attacker who ports the number can receive them. Authenticator apps and hardware keys are tied to the device.

questions.prompt: An administrator wants users' Documents folders to be stored on a file server automatically so they are backed up and follow users to any domain PC. Which Active Directory feature should be used?
questions.explanation: Folder redirection, set through Group Policy, points folders like Documents to a network location so the data lives on the server.

questions.prompt: An administrator wants to apply a Group Policy only to computers in the Sales department. How should the computer accounts be organized in Active Directory?
choices: Give each one a Sales prefix in its hostname
Add the computers to the Domain Admins group
Move them into a separate workgroup
Place them in a Sales OU and link the GPO to it
questions.explanation: GPOs are linked to sites, domains and OUs, so placing the computers in their own OU lets the policy target only them.

questions.prompt: A user sees advertising pop-ups in the Windows notification area even when the browser is closed. They started after the user clicked Allow on a website prompt. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Reinstall Windows and restore the user's files
Rebuild the user's profile from scratch
questions.explanation: Websites granted notification permission can push desktop alerts. Revoking the permission stops them without invasive steps.

questions.prompt: In CompTIA's malware removal procedure, which step comes immediately after disabling System Restore?
choices: Enable System Restore and create a restore point
questions.explanation: The order is investigate, quarantine, disable System Restore, remediate, schedule scans and update, re-enable System Restore, then educate the user.

questions.prompt: A technician wants a single timeline showing application crashes, Windows updates and other events on a PC over the past few weeks, with a stability score. Which tool should be used?
questions.explanation: Reliability Monitor plots a stability index over time and lists failures, warnings and software installs by day.

questions.prompt: After malware was removed from a PC, its browsers cannot load any websites, while other PCs on the network work. What should the technician check NEXT?
choices: Whether the switch port is disabled
Whether the monitor driver is current
Whether the DHCP server has stopped responding
Whether the proxy settings were changed
questions.explanation: Malware often sets a rogue proxy; once the malware is gone the proxy no longer works, so traffic fails until the setting is removed.

questions.prompt: On a new laptop with a 4K screen, Windows text and icons are too small for the user to read. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Change the refresh rate to 30 Hz
Install the generic Microsoft display driver
questions.explanation: Display scaling enlarges text and interface elements while keeping the native resolution, so the screen stays sharp.

questions.prompt: Every user on one PC lost the ability to print right after last night's Windows cumulative update. Other PCs that skipped the update work. What is the BEST quick fix?
choices: Replace the printer with a newer model
Uninstall that update and pause updates
Delete and recreate all user profiles
Reset the PC and remove everything
questions.explanation: When a problem starts right after a specific update, uninstalling it from Settings and pausing updates restores function until a fixed update is released.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to clean up toner that spilled inside a laser printer. What should be used?
choices: A can of compressed air only
Compressed air and a damp paper towel
questions.explanation: Toner particles are so fine they pass through ordinary vacuum filters and can melt or ignite in the motor, so a dedicated toner vacuum is used.

questions.prompt: A retail store processes customer credit card payments on its point-of-sale systems. Which standard defines how that card data must be protected?
questions.explanation: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard governs organizations that store, process or transmit cardholder data. HIPAA covers health information.

questions.prompt: A help desk needs a cross-platform tool to view and control the graphical desktops of Linux and macOS systems remotely. Which protocol is commonly used?
questions.explanation: Virtual Network Computing (VNC) provides remote graphical desktop control across many operating systems. Telnet and SFTP provide only text sessions or file transfer.

questions.prompt: Which file extension is typically used for a Linux Bash shell script?
questions.explanation: .sh is the conventional extension for shell scripts. .ps1 is PowerShell, .bat is Windows batch and .vbs is VBScript.

questions.prompt: A help desk wants every technician to install the company's accounting software using the same approved steps. Which document should be created?
questions.explanation: An SOP documents step-by-step instructions for a routine task so it is performed consistently.

questions.prompt: Instead of installing a large application on every PC, a company wants it to run on a central server and be delivered to users' desktops as if it were local. Which approach is this?
questions.explanation: Application virtualization or streaming runs or delivers individual apps from a central host without a full local installation or full virtual desktop.

questions.prompt: A user edits documents offline on a laptop, and the changes automatically appear on their phone and desktop after reconnecting. Which cloud feature provides this?
questions.explanation: File synchronization services such as OneDrive keep local copies on each device and sync changes through the cloud.

questions.prompt: A user with Windows 11 Home wants to enable the built-in Hyper-V feature to run virtual machines. What is required?
choices: Upgrade to Windows 11 Pro or Enterprise
Convert the disk from GPT to MBR
questions.explanation: Hyper-V is not included in Windows Home editions; it requires Pro, Enterprise or Education plus hardware virtualization support.

questions.prompt: A user wants to add more RAM to a thin ultrabook, but the specification sheet says it has 16 GB of LPDDR5 soldered to the motherboard. What should the technician tell the user?
choices: Enable virtual RAM in the UEFI to double capacity
Replace the soldered chips with larger LPDDR5 chips
It cannot be upgraded; buy a model with more RAM
Install a DDR5 SO-DIMM in the empty slot
questions.explanation: Soldered LPDDR memory has no slots, so capacity is fixed at purchase; the only practical option is a device configured with more RAM.

questions.prompt: A laptop's specification lists an M.2 2280 slot. What does the number 2280 describe?
choices: The drive holds up to 2,280 GB
The module is 22 mm wide and 80 mm long
The slot uses PCIe generation 2 with 280 pins
questions.explanation: M.2 size codes give width and length in millimetres, so 2280 means 22 mm by 80 mm; it says nothing about speed or capacity.

questions.prompt: A user with an iPhone 13 lost the charging cable that came with the phone. Which cable connector is needed on the phone end?
questions.explanation: iPhone models before the iPhone 15 use Apple's Lightning connector; Apple moved to USB-C starting with the iPhone 15.

questions.prompt: Government contractors must sign in to their laptops by inserting an ID badge that contains a certificate chip. Which accessory must each laptop have?
questions.explanation: A smart card reader reads the certificate stored on the chip of a badge such as a CAC or PIV card; NFC and magnetic stripe readers do not perform this certificate-based login.

questions.prompt: A new employee's company uses Google Workspace. They want their work email, calendar and contacts on their Android phone. What is the BEST way to set this up?
choices: Export contacts to a CSV file and copy it to the phone
Add their Google Workspace account in the phone's account settings
Configure POP3 so mail is downloaded and then deleted from the server
Forward all work email to a personal address
questions.explanation: Adding the Workspace account lets the phone synchronize mail, calendar and contacts with the server; POP3 would only download mail and would not sync calendars or contacts.

questions.prompt: A technician is ordering a replacement battery for a three-year-old business laptop. What BEST ensures the new battery is compatible?
choices: Choose the battery with the highest mAh rating available
Buy any battery that has the same physical length
Match the manufacturer's part number and voltage rating
Use the cheapest universal battery with an adapter
questions.explanation: Laptop batteries are model-specific, so matching the part number and voltage ensures correct fit, connector and charging behaviour; a higher capacity of the wrong type may not fit or charge safely.

questions.prompt: Besides the screen panel itself, which components are commonly housed in a laptop's display lid?
choices: CPU, RAM and the main cooling fan
questions.explanation: Laptop lids normally contain the Wi-Fi antenna leads, the webcam and often microphones, which is why they must be reconnected after a screen replacement.

questions.prompt: Which ports does SNMP use for manager polling requests and for agent trap messages?
questions.explanation: SNMP agents listen for queries on UDP 161, and managers receive unsolicited trap notifications on UDP 162.

questions.prompt: An office mail server must relay outgoing messages to other mail servers on the internet. Which port is used for server-to-server SMTP delivery?
questions.explanation: SMTP between mail servers uses TCP 25; 110 and 143 are POP3 and IMAP for mail retrieval, and 3389 is RDP.

questions.prompt: A homeowner wants smart locks and motion sensors that form their own low-power mesh network, separate from the home Wi-Fi. Which technology BEST fits?
questions.explanation: Zigbee is a low-power wireless mesh protocol designed for home automation devices; NFC and RFID work only at short range and LTE is a cellular service.

questions.prompt: A company wants all employee web requests to pass through a server that caches popular content and can block certain websites. Which server should be deployed?
questions.explanation: A proxy server makes requests on behalf of clients, which lets it cache content and filter which sites users may visit.

questions.prompt: An online store runs its website on four identical web servers and wants incoming requests spread evenly across them. Which device should be used?
questions.explanation: A load balancer distributes client requests among multiple servers to share the workload and improve availability.

questions.prompt: A small business wants one appliance that combines a firewall, intrusion prevention, antivirus scanning and content filtering. Which type of device is this?
questions.explanation: A UTM appliance bundles several security functions such as firewall, IPS, malware scanning and filtering into one device.

questions.prompt: A domain owner wants receiving mail servers to know whether to quarantine or reject messages that fail SPF and DKIM checks, and to send reports. Which DNS record should be published?
questions.explanation: DMARC is published as a TXT record and tells receivers how to handle mail that fails SPF or DKIM and where to send reports; MX only directs incoming mail.

questions.prompt: A DHCP scope hands out 192.168.10.10 through 192.168.10.200, but printers already use static addresses from .50 to .60. What should the administrator configure?
choices: A larger subnet mask on the scope
questions.explanation: An exclusion range stops the DHCP server from leasing addresses inside the scope that are already assigned statically, preventing IP conflicts.

questions.prompt: A rural business gets internet from a local provider that beams service from a nearby tower to a small antenna on its roof. Which connection type is this?
questions.explanation: A WISP delivers internet using fixed wireless links from towers to customer antennas; DSL and cable use phone and coaxial lines.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to passively copy all traffic on a network link to a monitoring device without interrupting the connection. Which tool should be installed inline?
questions.explanation: A network tap sits on a link and copies traffic to a monitoring port; a toner probe traces cables and a loopback plug tests ports.

questions.prompt: A water treatment plant uses networked systems to monitor and control pumps and valves at remote sites. What are these systems called?
questions.explanation: Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems monitor and control industrial equipment and often run legacy software that needs extra protection.

questions.prompt: A developer needs to run software compiled for a different CPU architecture than the host computer's processor. Which technology is required?
questions.explanation: Hypervisors and containers run code on the host's own CPU architecture, while an emulator translates instructions for a different architecture.

questions.prompt: A VM's virtual disk was created as dynamically expanding with a 500 GB maximum. Months later the host's physical drive unexpectedly runs out of space. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The VM switched to bridged networking
The virtual disk grew as data was added inside the VM
Snapshots were disabled on the VM
The hypervisor converted the disk to a fixed-size disk
questions.explanation: A dynamically expanding disk starts small and grows as the guest writes data, so the host can fill up if its free space is less than the maximum size.

questions.prompt: A company runs its servers on IaaS virtual machines from a cloud provider. Who is responsible for patching the guest operating systems?
questions.explanation: In IaaS the provider manages the physical hardware and virtualization layer, but the customer manages the operating systems and applications inside the VMs.

questions.prompt: A technician says a group of Windows VMs does not need antivirus or patching because they run inside a hypervisor. What is the BEST response?
choices: Only the host needs protection because it isolates the guests
Each VM needs the same updates and protection as a physical PC
Snapshots replace the need for security updates
VMs cannot be infected because they have no physical NIC
questions.explanation: A guest OS is exposed to the same malware and vulnerabilities as a physical system, so it must be patched and protected individually.

questions.prompt: A Mac user must run a Windows-only accounting application without giving up macOS. What is the BEST solution?
choices: Run Windows in a Type 2 hypervisor on the Mac
Change the Mac's startup disk file system to NTFS
Open the program in a Linux container
Install a Type 1 hypervisor and wipe macOS
questions.explanation: A Type 2 hypervisor runs as an application on macOS and can host a Windows VM for the accounting app while the user keeps macOS.

questions.prompt: Several VMs share one host. Whenever one VM runs a large nightly database job, the others become very slow. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The VMs are missing guest display drivers
The VMs are using host-only networking
questions.explanation: All VMs on a host draw from the same physical CPU, memory and storage, so one heavy workload can starve the others of resources.

questions.prompt: Which is the maximum data rate of USB 2.0 Hi-Speed?
questions.explanation: USB 2.0 Hi-Speed tops out at 480 Mbps; 12 Mbps is USB 1.1 Full Speed and 5 Gbps begins with USB 3.x.

questions.prompt: A user wants a single cable from a laptop to a dock that drives two 4K monitors and a fast external SSD. The laptop's USB-C port has a lightning bolt icon. Which interface does this port provide?
questions.explanation: The lightning bolt icon marks a Thunderbolt port, which uses the USB-C connector and provides up to 40 Gbps for displays, storage and docking.

questions.prompt: Which fiber optic connector is small form factor, uses a push-and-latch design, and is common on SFP transceiver modules?
questions.explanation: The LC (Lucent connector) is a small latching fiber connector widely used on SFP modules; ST uses a bayonet twist lock and F-type is for coaxial cable.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to connect a DSL modem to a telephone wall jack. Which connector does the cable use?
questions.explanation: Telephone and DSL lines use the smaller RJ11 connector; RJ45 is for Ethernet.

questions.prompt: A file server must keep running even if one of its power supplies fails. Which feature should be specified when purchasing it?
choices: A single higher-wattage power supply unit
questions.explanation: Redundant power supplies share the load so the server keeps running if one fails, and hot-swap lets the failed unit be replaced without shutting down.

questions.prompt: An older desktop with a manual input-voltage switch on its power supply is being shipped from the United States to an office in the United Kingdom. What should be done before plugging it in?
choices: Set the voltage switch to 230 V
Set the voltage switch to 115 V
questions.explanation: UK mains is about 230 V, so a manual-switch supply must be set to 230 V; leaving it on 115 V can destroy the power supply.

questions.prompt: A laser printer's display shows a message that it has reached 200,000 pages and needs scheduled service. What should the technician install?
questions.explanation: Laser printer maintenance kits replace wear parts such as the fuser and rollers at the page count set by the manufacturer.

questions.prompt: A graphic design team needs printed output that matches the on-screen layout exactly on complex, graphics-heavy pages. Which printer language driver is generally preferred?
questions.explanation: PostScript is device-independent and handles complex graphics and fonts accurately, which is why design teams usually prefer it; PCL is optimized for fast, general office printing.

questions.prompt: A warehouse prints shipping manifests on continuous paper with perforated holes along both edges. Which feed mechanism does the impact printer use?
questions.explanation: Tractor feed uses sprocket wheels that engage the holes on continuous-form paper, which is typical of impact printers.

questions.prompt: A dental lab needs a 3D printer that cures liquid material layer by layer with ultraviolet light to create very fine detail. Which type should it buy?
questions.explanation: Resin (SLA-type) 3D printers cure liquid resin with UV light and give finer detail than filament printers, which extrude melted plastic.

questions.prompt: A company needs dedicated tamper-resistant hardware to generate and store cryptographic keys for many servers. Which device should it use?
choices: A USB flash drive in a locked drawer
Trusted Platform Module on each desktop
questions.explanation: An HSM is a dedicated, tamper-resistant device for generating and protecting keys for multiple systems; a TPM protects keys for the single computer it is built into.

questions.prompt: A home studio user needs optical S/PDIF output and better audio quality than the motherboard's onboard audio provides. Which component should be installed?
questions.explanation: A sound card adds higher-quality audio processing and extra outputs such as optical S/PDIF; a capture card records incoming video.

questions.prompt: Every page from a laser printer has a sharp vertical black line in the same position. Which component is the MOST likely cause?
choices: A scratched or dirty imaging drum
A fuser that is not hot enough
questions.explanation: A scratch or debris on the drum attracts toner at the same spot on every rotation, producing a vertical line; a cold fuser instead lets toner rub off.

questions.prompt: Pages from a laser printer have random small black specks scattered across them. What should the technician do?
choices: Clean stray toner inside the printer
Reinstall the print driver on the PC
Lower the print resolution to 300 dpi
questions.explanation: Speckling usually comes from loose toner inside the printer or a leaking cartridge, so cleaning with a toner vacuum and checking the cartridge is the fix.

questions.prompt: A printer makes a loud grinding noise each time it tries to feed paper. What should the technician check FIRST?
choices: Whether the print spooler is running
Whether the toner level is low
questions.explanation: A grinding noise points to a mechanical problem, such as a foreign object, a jammed sheet or stripped gears in the feed path.

questions.prompt: A user's portrait documents keep printing sideways on the page from one application only. What should the technician check?
questions.explanation: Since only one application is affected, its page setup or print dialog is likely set to landscape; hardware faults would affect every application.

questions.prompt: A multifunction copier stopped stapling finished documents, although copies still come out correctly. What should be checked FIRST?
questions.explanation: Stapling is handled by the finisher, so an empty or jammed staple cartridge is the most likely cause when copying works normally.

questions.prompt: A switch log shows that the port connected to a user's PC goes up and down every few seconds, and the user's connection keeps dropping. What is this problem called?
questions.explanation: Port flapping is a link repeatedly going up and down, usually caused by a faulty cable, connector or NIC.

questions.prompt: A PC is running and its HDMI cable is connected to the graphics card, but the monitor shows a 'No input' message. What should be checked?
choices: Whether the CMOS battery is dead
Whether the network cable is unplugged
Whether the hard drive is failing
questions.explanation: Monitors with several inputs show 'No input' when set to a different source, so selecting the correct input is the quickest check.

questions.prompt: A PC is connected to a TV by HDMI. The picture works, but sound still plays from the PC's small speakers. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Make HDMI the default playback device
Replace the HDMI cable with a VGA cable
questions.explanation: HDMI carries audio, but Windows must be told to send sound to the HDMI output by making it the default playback device; VGA carries no audio.

questions.prompt: A new monitor has one pixel that always stays black no matter what is displayed. What is this called?
questions.explanation: A dead pixel never lights at all, while a stuck pixel stays lit in one color.

questions.prompt: A storage server's hot-swap drive bay shows an amber status LED, while the other bays show green. What does this MOST likely indicate?
choices: That drive is the fastest in the array
That drive has failed or may fail soon
That drive is receiving extra power
questions.explanation: Drive bay LEDs usually show green for normal activity and amber for a fault or predicted failure, marking the drive to replace.

questions.prompt: Users of a database server complain about slow queries. Monitoring shows long read and write times and low IOPS on its mechanical hard drives. What is the BEST upgrade?
choices: Replace the hard drives with SSDs
questions.explanation: SSDs deliver far more IOPS and lower latency than mechanical drives, which directly addresses slow storage performance.

questions.prompt: A laptop shows a 'slow charger' warning and its battery drains during heavy use while plugged into a small USB-C phone charger. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The charger's wattage is too low
The USB-C port is in data-only mode
The display brightness is too high
The battery firmware needs a reset
questions.explanation: Laptops need far more power than phones, so a low-wattage charger cannot keep up with demand; the fix is a charger that meets the laptop's rated wattage.

questions.prompt: A technician tested a theory and confirmed what caused a problem. According to the CompTIA troubleshooting methodology, what is the NEXT step?
choices: Question the user and identify recent changes
Verify full system functionality and implement preventive measures
Establish a plan of action and implement the solution
questions.explanation: After the theory is confirmed, the technician plans and implements the fix; verifying functionality and documenting come afterward.

questions.prompt: A desktop that worked yesterday no longer gets an IP address, and the technician finds the NIC port on the back of the PC has a bent and broken pin. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Reset the switch to factory defaults
questions.explanation: A physically damaged port cannot make a reliable connection, so the adapter must be replaced, for example with an add-in or USB NIC.

questions.prompt: A user reports that a cloud application is slow, and the technician wants hop-by-hop statistics showing packet loss at each router along the path over time. Which Windows command should be used?
questions.explanation: pathping combines ping and tracert, sending packets to each hop over a period and reporting the loss and latency at every router.

questions.prompt: At a Windows command prompt, which command creates a new folder named Reports in the current directory?
questions.explanation: md (or mkdir) makes a directory; cd changes into a directory, rd removes one and dir lists contents.

questions.prompt: A user opened an email attachment named invoice.pdf that turned out to be a program. The technician wants users to see the real file type in File Explorer. Which setting should be changed?
choices: Change the default app for PDF files
Show extensions for known file types
Show hidden and protected system files
questions.explanation: Windows hides known extensions by default, so a file named invoice.pdf.exe appears as invoice.pdf; showing extensions reveals the true type.

questions.prompt: A USB barcode scanner on a desktop stops responding after a few minutes of inactivity and works again after being unplugged. Which Power Options setting should the technician disable?
questions.explanation: USB selective suspend lets Windows power down idle USB devices, which can cause some devices to stop responding until reconnected.

questions.prompt: Which Windows Power Options feature saves the kernel session to disk at shutdown so the PC boots faster the next time?
questions.explanation: Fast startup performs a hybrid shutdown that writes the kernel session to the hibernation file, which speeds up the next boot.

questions.prompt: A traveller wants their laptop to save all open work to disk and power off completely so it uses no battery during a long flight, then resume where they left off. Which power state should they use?
questions.explanation: Hibernate writes the contents of RAM to disk and turns the system off, while sleep keeps RAM powered and continues to use some battery.

questions.prompt: Windows search on a user's PC no longer finds files that are definitely in the Documents folder. Which Control Panel tool should the technician use to fix this?
choices: Programs and Features, to repair Office
Internet Options, to clear temporary files
Indexing Options, to rebuild the index
Device Manager, to update the disk driver
questions.explanation: Windows search relies on the index, and rebuilding it in Indexing Options fixes missing or out-of-date search results.

questions.prompt: A Linux administrator wants a second drive to be mounted automatically at /data every time the system boots. Which file should be edited?
questions.explanation: /etc/fstab lists the file systems to mount at boot and their mount points; /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow hold account data and /etc/hosts maps names to IP addresses.

questions.prompt: A Linux technician wants to query DNS directly and see detailed information about the records returned for a domain. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: dig queries DNS servers and shows detailed answers for record lookups; chown changes ownership, df shows disk space and pwd prints the current directory.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command displays the contents of a text file in the terminal?
questions.explanation: cat outputs a file's contents to the screen; cp copies files, rm removes them and ls lists directory contents.

questions.prompt: A Mac user downloads software that comes as an installer package with a step-by-step setup wizard. Which file extension does this package use?
questions.explanation: macOS installer packages use the .pkg extension and run through the Installer app; .exe and .msi are Windows formats and .apk is for Android.

questions.prompt: A company needs to set up 200 new laptops with the same operating system, applications and settings as quickly as possible. Which method is BEST?
choices: Have each user install their own applications
Deploy a prepared standard image to each laptop
Perform a manual clean install on each laptop
Do an in-place upgrade on each laptop
questions.explanation: Image deployment copies one tested configuration to many machines quickly and consistently, which is far faster than installing each system by hand.

questions.prompt: A CAD application requires a dedicated graphics card with 8 GB of VRAM, but an engineer's desktop has only integrated graphics. What should the technician do before installing the application?
choices: Install the 32-bit version of the app
Add a second monitor to the desktop
questions.explanation: Integrated graphics shares system memory and does not meet a dedicated VRAM requirement, so a discrete graphics card is needed for the application to run properly.

questions.prompt: During a Windows clean install on a new workstation, setup shows no drives on which to install, although the NVMe drive works in the UEFI. What should the technician do?
choices: Convert the drive to MBR in the UEFI
Replace the NVMe drive with a larger one
Use Load driver to add the storage driver
questions.explanation: When setup cannot see a drive, it usually lacks a driver for the storage or RAID controller, which can be loaded from USB during installation.

questions.prompt: A PC is infected with malware that loads before the operating system by hiding in the startup code at the beginning of the drive. Which type of malware is this?
questions.explanation: A boot sector virus infects the boot record so it runs before the OS loads, which makes it hard for normal antivirus scans to remove.

questions.prompt: Attackers infect a trade association website that employees of a target company often visit, hoping to compromise their PCs. What is this attack called?
questions.explanation: A watering hole attack compromises a site the targets are known to visit rather than attacking them directly.

questions.prompt: An employee who has resigned copies the customer database to a personal USB drive on their last day. Which type of threat does this represent?
questions.explanation: An insider threat comes from someone with legitimate access, such as an employee, who misuses it.

questions.prompt: Attackers compromised a software vendor and inserted malicious code into a legitimate update that thousands of customers installed. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: A supply chain attack targets a trusted supplier so the malicious code reaches victims through normal, trusted channels such as updates.

questions.prompt: A technician hardening a SOHO router finds a feature that lets devices on the LAN open inbound ports automatically without administrator approval. Which feature should be disabled?
questions.explanation: Universal Plug and Play lets devices and malware create port forwards automatically, so disabling it keeps control of inbound access with the administrator.

questions.prompt: A small office wants to host a public game server while keeping it separated from the internal LAN. Which SOHO router feature should be used?
questions.explanation: A screened subnet (formerly called a DMZ) places internet-facing hosts in a separate zone so a compromise does not give direct access to the internal network.

questions.prompt: A small business wants to stop employees on the office network from reaching gambling and adult websites. Which SOHO router feature should be configured?
questions.explanation: Content filtering blocks websites by category, keyword or address list, which enforces acceptable use on the network.

questions.prompt: A technician performs a quick format on a used drive before giving it to another department. Why is this NOT enough to protect the old data?
choices: Quick formats only work on SSDs
The data moves to a hidden partition
The format encrypts data with a known key
The old data can still be recovered
questions.explanation: A standard quick format only rebuilds the file system and marks the space as free, so recovery software can still read the old files; wiping or destruction is needed.

questions.prompt: A company issues employees small key fobs that show a new six-digit code every 30 seconds for logging in to the VPN. What is this an example of?
questions.explanation: A hardware token is a physical device that generates one-time codes; a soft token is an authenticator app on a phone or computer.

questions.prompt: A company wants to prevent warehouse staff accounts from signing in to the domain outside their scheduled shifts. Which account control should be configured?
questions.explanation: Logon hour restrictions limit when an account can sign in, reducing the window an attacker could use a stolen account.

questions.prompt: Users in an office keep installing unapproved software on their Windows PCs. Which change BEST prevents this?
choices: Enable Remote Desktop on every PC
Turn off Windows Update on each PC
questions.explanation: Standard users cannot install most software or change system settings without administrator credentials, which enforces least privilege.

questions.prompt: A user copies a file from a folder where only HR can read it into a public shared folder on the same NTFS volume. What permissions will the copy have?
choices: It loses all permissions and cannot be opened
It becomes readable only by administrators
questions.explanation: A copied file is a new file, so it takes on the inherited permissions of the destination folder, which can expose sensitive data placed in a public share.

questions.prompt: An employee reports a company phone lost somewhere in the city. The MDM shows it is still powered on. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Wait a week to see if it is returned
Locate the phone and remotely lock it
Reset only the user's domain password
questions.explanation: A locator app can show where the device is and lock it remotely; if it cannot be recovered, a remote wipe protects the company's data.
