questions.prompt: A company wants an electronic record of exactly who entered the server room and at what time. Which physical control BEST provides this?
choices: A sign on the door saying Authorized Only
A badge reader access system with logging
questions.explanation: Badge readers tie each entry to an individual credential and log the time, while a shared key gives no record of who opened the door.

questions.prompt: When a user plugs a USB webcam into a hub with several other devices, Windows displays a 'Not enough USB controller resources' message. What should the technician try FIRST?
choices: Use a port on a different USB controller
Replace the webcam with a Bluetooth model
Reinstall Windows and the USB drivers
questions.explanation: The message means one controller has run out of endpoints or bandwidth, so moving the device to a port on another controller, often a rear port, or removing devices from the hub resolves it.

questions.prompt: Windows Update repeatedly fails to install a feature update, and the PC's system drive has only 2 GB free. What should the technician do FIRST?
choices: Reinstall all of the device drivers
Free up space on the drive and retry
Replace the RAM with faster modules
questions.explanation: Feature updates need significant free space to download and install, so clearing space on the system drive is the first fix.

questions.prompt: An MDM report shows that an employee's Android phone has developer options and USB debugging enabled. What is the BEST action?
choices: Disable them, as they weaken security
Root the phone to finish the setup
Leave them on to improve battery life
questions.explanation: Developer mode and USB debugging allow deeper access to the device and can be abused to install or extract data, so they should be off on corporate phones.

questions.prompt: A user tries to install a required business app on an older phone, but the app store says the app is not compatible with the device. What should be checked FIRST?
choices: Whether the case is blocking the antenna
The app's minimum OS version requirement
Whether the screen brightness is too low
questions.explanation: Apps specify a minimum OS version, so updating the operating system, or replacing a phone that can no longer be updated, is usually required.

questions.prompt: An Android phone has started rebooting randomly since the user installed several new apps. Which step BEST helps determine whether a third-party app is responsible?
choices: Turn off location services for a full day
Remove and reinsert the SIM card
Boot into safe mode and watch for reboots
questions.explanation: Android safe mode loads only the preinstalled apps, so if the problem stops there, a downloaded app is the likely cause and can be uninstalled.

questions.prompt: A user cannot pay at a store by tapping their phone, though the payment card is set up in the wallet app. What should be checked FIRST?
choices: NFC status and the default wallet app
That airplane mode is turned on
That the phone's GPS is turned off
questions.explanation: Tap-to-pay uses NFC, so the NFC radio must be on and the correct wallet set as the default payment app.

questions.prompt: A user downloads what appears to be their bank's app from a link in a text message, but it is published by an unknown developer and asks for their banking password. What is the MOST likely issue?
choices: An expired SSL certificate on the phone
A spoofed app impersonating the bank
questions.explanation: App spoofing uses lookalike apps to steal credentials, so users should install apps only from official stores and check the publisher name.

questions.prompt: After a malware infection was cleaned, a PC can ping IP addresses on the internet but cannot resolve any website names. Other PCs work fine. What should the technician check?
questions.explanation: Malware often points DNS to rogue servers, so if names fail while IP connectivity works, the adapter's DNS settings should be checked and reset.

questions.prompt: A standard corporate laptop has had repeated OS corruption that sfc, DISM and System Restore could not fix. The user's files are stored on network shares. What is the MOST efficient fix?
choices: Reimage it with the standard image
Keep running sfc until it succeeds
questions.explanation: When repairs fail and data is safely stored elsewhere, reimaging returns the laptop to a known good configuration quickly.

questions.prompt: A user's new 64-bit only application refuses to install on their PC, which shows it is running a 32-bit edition of Windows. What is the fix?
choices: Run the installer in compatibility mode
Add more RAM to the PC first
questions.explanation: 64-bit applications cannot run on a 32-bit OS, so the system must be reinstalled with a 64-bit edition on a 64-bit capable CPU.

questions.prompt: A user notices that some of their Word documents now contain text they did not write, and several system files have recent modification dates. Which issue should the technician suspect FIRST?
questions.explanation: Unexpected changes to personal or system files are a common sign of malware, so the technician should begin the malware removal process.

questions.prompt: A legacy Windows logon script has a .vbs extension. Which scripting language is it written in?
questions.explanation: .vbs files are VBScript, run by Windows Script Host; PowerShell uses .ps1, Python .py and Bash .sh.

questions.prompt: A technician finds a handy script on a public forum and wants to run it on all company PCs. What should be done FIRST?
choices: Email it to users to run themselves
Rename it to .txt to make it safe
Review and test it in a sandbox first
Run it immediately on every PC to save time
questions.explanation: Unknown scripts can introduce malware, change system settings unexpectedly or crash systems by mishandling resources, so they must be reviewed and tested first.

questions.prompt: A clinic's database stores patients' diagnoses, treatment records and insurance details. Which type of regulated data is this?
questions.explanation: Medical records linked to an individual are PHI, which has strict legal requirements for privacy and protection.

questions.prompt: A company's legal department says certain financial records must be kept for seven years and then securely destroyed. Which policy does this describe?
questions.explanation: A data retention policy states how long each type of data must be kept to meet legal or regulatory requirements and how it is disposed of afterward.

questions.prompt: An employee installs software bought under a personal, home-use licence on their company workstation. What is the main issue?
choices: The licence does not permit business or corporate use
The software will automatically become open source
The licence makes the PC exempt from updates
Personal licences only run on Linux
questions.explanation: Personal licences usually prohibit commercial use, so the company must obtain a proper corporate licence to stay compliant.

questions.prompt: A user purchased e-books on one reading app and finds they cannot open them in a different app or copy them to a colleague. What technology causes this?
questions.explanation: DRM restricts how purchased digital content can be copied, shared or used, often tying it to a specific account or app.

questions.prompt: An IT team needs a database that records servers, software and network devices along with how they depend on each other. What is this called?
questions.explanation: A CMDB stores configuration items and the relationships between them, which helps assess the impact of changes and incidents.

questions.prompt: An employee leaves the company today. Which document BEST ensures IT disables their accounts, collects their equipment and revokes their access?
questions.explanation: An offboarding (termination) checklist makes sure every account, device and access right is handled consistently when someone leaves.

questions.prompt: A tier 1 help desk technician cannot resolve a complex server issue within the allowed time. What should the technician do?
choices: Keep working on it without updating the ticket
Close the ticket and ask the user to call back
Tell the user the problem cannot be fixed
Escalate it to the next tier with notes
questions.explanation: Escalation passes the issue to staff with more expertise, and clear notes on what was already tried prevent duplicated work.

questions.prompt: A company wants staff to use generative AI to summarize confidential contracts. Which approach BEST protects the data?
choices: Have staff use personal AI accounts
Use any free public chatbot service
Use a private, company-managed AI service
Remove page numbers before uploading files
questions.explanation: A private or enterprise AI deployment keeps data under the company's control, while public AI tools may store or reuse what users submit.

questions.prompt: A technician removes a RAM module from a working PC and needs to store it until it is reinstalled next week. How should it be stored?
questions.explanation: Antistatic bags shield components from electrostatic discharge, which can damage memory even when no damage is visible.
